name: MIMIC-IV: Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV
description: MIMIC-IV is the contemporary, premier relational electronic health record (EHR) database developed by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC), published in Nature Scientific Data. Spanning over a decade of clinical care (2008–2019), MIMIC-IV documents the comprehensive hospital journeys of over 300,000 distinct patients admitted to emergency departments and intensive care units. Structured across modular clinical domains (core, hosp, icu, ed), the database contains de-identified tables capturing admissions, patient demographics, laboratory blood chemistry and hematology tests, provider orders, medication administration records, vital signs, procedural interventions, and ICD-9/ICD-10 diagnostic billing codes.

license.notes: Governed by PhysioNet Credentialed/Restricted Health Data License 1.5.0, which restricts use to the "sole purpose of lawful use in scientific research and no other". While commercial data resale, unauthorized redistribution, and product deployment are strictly prohibited, whether bona fide scientific research conducted by commercial/industry investigators under institutional credentialing is permitted remains an unstated legal question. Commercial permission is recorded as unknown.
